findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify whether BLANK separator units are absorbed into a contiguous SAFE run (and how they re-materialize as blank lines in the single combined Markdown document) or break the run, so the batching actually fires for realistic blank-separated multi-paragraph bodies.
evidence: Plan: 'groups each maximal run of contiguous SAFE units and feeds it to pandoc as one Markdown document'
wiki_render.py:164-168 emits a standalone (_BLANK, ...) unit for each blank-line separator, so _RENDER units are typically separated by a _BLANK unit rather than being directly adjacent
ABSENCE: plan never states whether BLANK units are absorbed into a safe run or break it, nor how absorbed blanks re-materialize as blank lines in the single combined Markdown document
findings.finding: The batching mechanism ('maximal run of contiguous SAFE units') does not define whether the BLANK separator units that 271c's _lock_and_split emits between two SAFE (_RENDER) units break run contiguity; if blanks break the run, contiguous SAFE runs of length>1 almost never occur and the batching optimization is a silent no-op that fails to solve the per-field spawn-tax hazard it targets.
scenarios: A body of N paragraphs each separated by a blank line: if blanks break runs, every paragraph is its own run and the plan spawns N pandoc processes — the exact per-field tax it set out to eliminate
findings.suggested_fix: State that a run absorbs interleaved BLANK units (re-emitting their exact text as blank lines between safe blocks in the one Markdown document), so a run breaks only at a TABLE/EXACT/dangerous unit; then a chain of paragraphs separated by blanks is one invocation.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the parenthetical: pandoc 3.x DOES have a persistent `pandoc-server` HTTP/CGI mode; justify choosing contiguous-safe-run batching over it on accurate grounds (e.g. the pypandoc-binary wheel does not ship/symlink the pandoc-server entrypoint, and adding an HTTP/CGI surface is undesirable), rather than by falsely asserting no server exists.
evidence: Plan quote: '(pandoc 3.9 exposes no `--server`/daemon, so a persistent server is out of scope.)'
Retrieved pandoc.org/pandoc-server.html: 'pandoc-server is a web server that can perform pandoc conversions. It can be used either as a running server or as a CGI program.'
Retrieved pandoc.org/installing.html: 'server: compile in support for running in HTTP server mode when the executable is renamed (or symlinked as) pandoc-server.'
The dismissal is load-bearing: it forecloses the one prior-art option that directly attacks hazard (1)'s '~0.3s/field spawn cost'.
findings.finding: The plan dismisses the persistent-server prior-art alternative with an inaccurate capability assertion: 'pandoc 3.9 exposes no --server/daemon, so a persistent server is out of scope.' Pandoc's 3.x line DOES ship a persistent server mode — `pandoc-server`, a long-running HTTP conversion service (default port 3030), also usable as a CGI program — documented at pandoc.org/pandoc-server.html and in jgm/pandoc. A persistent server is the canonical way to eliminate per-conversion process-spawn cost, which is exactly hazard (1) this story targets, so the alternative deserves an accurate comparison rather than dismissal on a false premise.
findings.location: Approach — 'Batch contiguous SAFE units' bullet (parenthetical); Context/Problem hazard (1)
scenarios: A reviewer or future maintainer questions why batching (not a persistent server) was chosen and finds the stated reason is factually wrong.
The pypandoc-binary wheel turns out to ship (or can symlink) the pandoc-server entrypoint, reopening the dismissed option.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the parenthetical with an accurate trade-off, e.g.: 'pandoc ships a persistent HTTP server (`pandoc-server`), but the pinned `pypandoc-binary` wheel delivers only the plain `pandoc` executable (no `pandoc-server` entrypoint) and adding a long-running HTTP/CGI surface is out of scope; contiguous-safe-run batching bounds spawn cost within the existing one-shot invocation model.' Confirm the wheel's shipped contents before finalizing the wording.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that test_dc_pandoc_timeout_falls_back exercises a REAL process group (a child that spawns a grandchild which outlives a naive child-only kill) so it actually proves rebar._proc.reap_process_group killpg-reaps the surviving grandchild, rather than mocking Popen/the timeout.
evidence: Plan: 'a plain subprocess.run(timeout=)/pypandoc timeout reaps only the DIRECT child, so a pandoc jira-reader spinning at ~95.8% CPU (a pipe-holding grandchild) survives'
Plan: 'verified by test_dc_pandoc_timeout_falls_back (asserts the group is reaped)' — but the test does not state it spawns a real child-that-spawns-a-surviving-grandchild
E5 proxy-validation: a risky new path validated solely through a substitute that bypasses the real boundary is a MAJOR gap
findings.finding: The timeout/reaping acceptance test (test_dc_pandoc_timeout_falls_back, 'asserts the group is reaped') does not specify HOW the CPU-spinning pipe-holding grandchild is produced. The entire robustness thesis is that a naive subprocess timeout reaps only the direct child while the grandchild survives (repo bug d843 / bpo-30154). If the test mocks Popen or stubs the timeout rather than spawning a real process group that actually orphans a grandchild, it validates the fallback branch without ever proving reap_process_group kills the surviving grandchild — the exact production failure mode goes untested (proxy-validation).
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria bullet 1 / Scope tests — 'test_dc_pandoc_timeout_falls_back (asserts the group is reaped)'
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the test spec: launch a small real command (e.g. a shim that forks a sleeping/spinning grandchild holding the stdout pipe) under start_new_session=True, trigger the caller-side communicate(timeout=) path, and assert (via os.killpg(pgid,0)→ProcessLookupError or /proc absence) that the grandchild PID is gone after reap — not merely that fallback text was returned.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define wiki_render.py-local grace/drain constants (or source them from the stdlib-leaf/config layer) rather than reusing adapters/jira/'s _ACLI_* constants, to respect the ADR-0083 vendor-adapter seam that wiki_render.py already documents.
evidence: Plan: "'grace'/'drain' reuse the ACLI caller's existing constants"
acli_subprocess.py:68-69 defines _ACLI_GRACE_SECONDS/_ACLI_DRAIN_SECONDS in adapters/jira/
wiki_render.py:41-42 docstring: 'Per docs/adr/0083-reconciler-vendor-adapter-seam.md this package imports nothing from adapters/jira/'
findings.finding: The plan reuses the ACLI caller's grace/drain constants, but those constants (_ACLI_GRACE_SECONDS/_ACLI_DRAIN_SECONDS) live in adapters/jira/acli_subprocess.py, and wiki_render.py (adapters/jira_family/) is barred by ADR 0083 from importing adapters/jira/; the plan gives no seam-respecting source for these values.
findings.location: Approach — 'grace/drain reuse the ACLI caller's existing constants'; Scope — wiki_render.py
scenarios: Implementer literally imports the ACLI constants from acli_subprocess into wiki_render.py, breaching the documented vendor-adapter seam
findings.suggested_fix: Add module-local constants in wiki_render.py (e.g. _DC_PANDOC_GRACE_S/_DC_PANDOC_DRAIN_S) and pass them to reap_process_group with label='dc-pandoc'; do not import from adapters/jira/.
